data_requests.item: Existing steam-trap identity, service and inventory/program coverage
where: site records: Existing named trap/service inventory, represented versus actual population, pressure ranges, inspection/maintenance dates and coverage; retain each source/revision, availability and authority limits.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: Establish steam-trap service before applying steam guidance; known grease/oil/sand/air traps are not steam traps, and ambiguous TRAP/ST labels need conditional service review. The source500-trap and3–5year loss examples are not universal program thresholds or actual population/failure estimates. Its pressure-dependent intervals are source guidance to review in context, not automatic site schedules.

data_requests.item: Existing qualified inspection results and remaining uncertainty
where: site records: Existing per-trap testing methods, service/pressure and operating conditions, observed condition with uncertainty, repair/retest/report history and unresolved coverage.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: Review suitable existing records before any new field survey. Temperature, sound, visual or electronic indications require service/method interpretation and do not turn a symbol into failed-open/closed truth. Preserve unknown or foreign results for each candidate; one survey cannot clear another source/population. A suitable current program may be acknowledged without a new measurement or blanket retrofit.

questions.decision_rule: Review the applicable steam-trap service, pressure, importance and existing inspection/repair reporting coverage with the responsible engineer. No universal500-trap or3–5year cutoff establishes whether a program is worthwhile, current, complete or unnecessary, and historical source failure percentages are not this site's condition. Acknowledge suitable existing program or nonapplicability; retain missing identity, method or coverage as a records question rather than a compulsory survey or failure diagnosis.

typical_benefit.wording: Unmaintained 3-5 years: "between 15% to 30% of the installed steam traps may have failed." With a program, "less than 5%." LBNL refinery table (as reported in LBNL-56183): trap maintenance 10-15% fuel saved, 0.5 yr payback.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.2113 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 445 recommendations, 0.6 yr average payback, 80.1% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S3: Steam Tip #1, Inspect and Repair Steam Traps (DOE/GO-102012-3401)
S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers. Source review: complete S3 pp1–2 includes systematic reporting, testing-method qualification and pressure-dependent suggested intervals. Represented count is not installed population. S19/S24 figures are inherited historical context, not reverified here or transferred to a site.
